newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BA fare rise under three pct - Marshall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BA fare rise under three pct - Marshall.

text.p: British Airways Plc (BA) chairman Sir Colin Marshall said on Monday that BA was likely to seek fare increases of less than three percent because BA was less affected by rising fuel prices than some other airlines.

"That's quite likely," Marshall told reporters when asked if BA's fare increases would be less than the three percent agreed by world airlines last week. He said the strength of sterling against the dollar had meant BA was less affected by the recent rise in fuel prices, which are denominated in U.S. dollars.

Last Friday, the world's airlines proposed a global three percent passenger fare increase to make up for a surge of more than 40 percent in fuel costs this year, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said in Geneva.
The 251-member airlines body said the proposed increase, which is subject to government approvals, would apply to fares from December 15.
But Marshall said the extent to which the three percent increase was applied depended on each individual carrier and how fuel prices changed through the northern hemisphere's winter.
"We're all watching what's likely to happen over these next few weeks from the weather standpoint, because that, to some extent, determines what does happen," he said.
BA had already raised some fares by about one percent a few weeks ago to at least partically compensate for the higher fuel prices, he said.
"You also have to bear in mind that the impact for individual carriers does depend on exchange rates in that all aviation fuel is priced in U.S. dollar terms," he said.
"So one has to watch what is happening to your own currency versus the U.S. dollar to see what the overall impact will be for a company," he said.
"The pound has been relatively strong against the dollar and that's why we only applied about a one percent increase in price."
